Jordan's Oil & Gas Producers Hit by 2021 Ransomware Attack

In late August 2021, the Oil & Gas Producers industry in Jordan faced a significant cyber security incident, as several leading firms were targeted by a coordinated ransomware attack. Among those affected was Jordan Petroleum Refinery Co, which confirmed that its internal IT systems had been compromised, leading to a temporary disruption of some administrative operations.

The attack, believed to have been executed by a sophisticated criminal group, encrypted key company files and demanded payment in cryptocurrency for decryption. While production facilities remained largely unaffected, operations such as procurement, payroll, and logistics experienced delays. At the peak of the incident, an estimated 15% of sector employees were unable to access key digital tools, according to figures provided by the Jordan Oil & Gas Association.

“Immediate action was taken to contain the threat and restore our systems from backup,” said Saad Al-Masri, IT Director at Jordan Petroleum Refinery Co. “We engaged with national cyber security authorities and implemented new protocols to prevent future incidents.”

Operations were fully restored within 10 days, and no long-term impact on fuel supply was reported. However, the event underscored the sector’s vulnerability to cyber threats. “The 2021 incident was a wake-up call for the industry,” commented energy analyst Lina Haddad. “It spurred investment in cyber resilience and drove collaborative efforts to share threat intelligence among operators.”

A subsequent review by the Jordan Oil & Gas Association led to sector-wide recommendations for enhanced encryption, employee training, and regular system audits. According to the association, no disruptions have been reported since the event, and companies continue to bolster their defenses against evolving threats.
